# getTriggerById

<link-summary>Finds one of the project's triggers by its id.</link-summary>

<web-summary>getTriggerById() — Finds one of the project's triggers by its id. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function getTriggerById(id: string): GoogleAppsScript.Script.Trigger | null;
```

Apps Script hands out a trigger id when a trigger is created but offers no way to look one up again, so the project's triggers are walked and compared. A trigger that has since been deleted gives `null`, which is the case a stored id has to handle.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description                           |
| :-------- | :------- | :------------------------------------ |
| `id`      | `string` | The trigger id. It must not be empty. |

## Returns

`GoogleAppsScript.Script.Trigger | null` — the trigger, or `null` when the project has none with that id.

## Throws

| Exception              | Condition                            |
| :--------------------- | :----------------------------------- |
| `EmptyStringException` | the id is not a string, or is empty. |

## Examples

### Looking up

```javascript
const id = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty("TRIGGER_ID");

const trigger = getTriggerById(id);

if (trigger !== null) {
  ScriptApp.deleteTrigger(trigger);
}
```
